sentences.text:
This application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner, in connection with FIR No.156/2022 registered at Police Station Kotwali Nimbahera,
District Chittorgarh, for offences under Sections 420, 406 and 120-B IPC.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as per prosecution, the petitioner despite having entered into an agreement dated 27.10.2022 with the complainant and one Bharat to sell them 1/5th portion of the property bearing Araji Nos.2213, 2214 and 2215 situated in Nimbahera, for a consideration of Rs.25,00,000/-, sold the property in question to a third party namely Pushpa through a registered sale deed on 28.2.2022.

Learned counsel submitted that further allegation against the petitioner is that an advance consideration of [2023:RJ-JD:30600] (2 of 3)
[CRLMB-10451/2023] Rs.5,00,000/- was taken by the petitioner and the same has not been returned to the complainant till date.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that after making agreement to sale with the complainant, the petitioner due to urgent need of money had to sell the property to someone else, because the complainant was not ready to pay the remaining consideration prior to the last date mentioned in the agreement i.e. January 2023.

Learned counsel submitted that earlier, the petitioner preferred S.B.Cr.Misc. Petition No.2780/2022 Chandi Bai @

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner has always shown her willingness to return the advance received by her towards aforementioned agreement dated 27.10.2022.
However, the same has not been accepted by the complainant and only with a view to give a pure civil dispute between the parties a colour of criminal case, the impugned FIR has been lodged.
Learned counsel thus, prayed that the petitioner may be granted anticipatory bail.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application and submitted that the petitioner since the very beginning had intention to cheat the complainant and therefore, the petitioner despite accepting advance amount, sold the property to third party.
Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- which had been received in advance by the petitioner has not been returned till date.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

[2023:RJ-JD:30600] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-10451/2023] Having considered rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case and upon a consideration of the arguments advanced at the bar that petitioner is ready and willing to pay the amount of Rs.5,00,000/- which he had received in advance coupled with the fact that the custodial interrogation of the present petitioner is not necessitated in the present case, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner under Section 438 Cr.P.C.
that the petitioner shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as per prosecution, the petitioner despite having entered into an agreement dated 27.10.2022 with the complainant and one Bharat to sell them 1/5th portion of the property bearing Araji Nos.2213, 2214 and 2215 situated in Nimbahera, for a consideration of Rs.25,00,000/-, sold the property in question to a third party namely Pushpa through a registered sale deed on 28.2.2022.

Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner has always shown her willingness to return the advance received by her towards aforementioned agreement dated 27.10.2022.
However, the same has not been accepted by the complainant and only with a view to give a pure civil dispute between the parties a colour of criminal case, the impugned FIR has been lodged.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, the bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that in the event of arrest of the petitioner- Smt. Chandi Bai W/o Ramesh in connection with FIR No.156/2022 registered at Police Station Kotwali Nimbahera, District Chittorgarh, the petitioner shall be released on bail; provided she furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the concerned investigating officer/S.H.O. on the following conditions:
(i). that the petitioner shall make herself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii). that the petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or any police officer; and (iii).
that the petitioner shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.
